summary: The exposure-prioritized successor probe saw the new disjoint C/C++ abstention rows but regressed the strict holdout sharply, so the current weakness-repair path should not be promoted.

interpretation.ordering_hypothesis: supported only in the narrow sense that the prioritized rows were definitely exposed during training
interpretation.improvement_hypothesis: falsified on the current capped probe; prioritized exposure made the holdout worse
interpretation.current_frontier_statement: The added disjoint C/C++ abstention-only rows are not a direct multilingual repair lever under the current bounded-decoder objective.
interpretation.web_status: Still blocked on fresh source-backed roots. No disjoint reviewed web root remains safe for compact-bounded train support without eval leakage.

anti_cheat_relevance: The web gap is not honestly fixable by replaying reviewed roots because all reviewed web roots overlap the current miss frontier.
The C/C++ abstention rows came from a rejected underconstrained bundle and are suitable only as train-only honesty support, not same-surface scoring evidence.
A negative result here is valuable: it shows the 100M was not merely failing because the rows were unseen; the objective/exposure interaction is also misaligned.

do_not_promote: Do not promote the Stage10256 runtime bundle.
Do not continue identical short capped replay on this package.
Do not interpret the C/C++ abstention support as a multilingual win path.
